<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, toRef, useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeSortableList, useDnD } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';
import StoryCard from './StoryCard.vue';

type Story = { id: string; title: string; points: number; bug?: boolean };
const props = defineProps<{ column: { id: string; title: string; stories: Story[] }; wholeColumn: boolean }>();

const zone = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('zone');
const list = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('list');
// Same `group`: stories move between the two lists. `dropzone`: the element that takes
// drops for the list, here the whole column (a getter, so the switch applies at once).
const { items, isOver } = makeSortableList(list, {
  id: props.column.id,
  items: toRef(props.column, 'stories'),
  group: 'planning',
  dropzone: () => (props.wholeColumn ? zone.value : undefined),
});

const points = computed(() => props.column.stories.reduce((sum, story) => sum + story.points, 0));
const { active } = useDnD();
</script>

<template>

    </h3>
    <ul ref="list" class="stories" :class="{ area: !wholeColumn }">

import { reactive } from 'vue';
import type { Key } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

export interface Guest {
  id: string;
  name: string;
}

export interface Seating {
  state: { tables: Record<Key, Guest[]>; history: { label: string; before: [Key, Guest[]][] }[] };
  apply(result: ReadonlyMap<Key, Guest[]>, label: string): void;
  undo(): void;
}

/**
 * A small store: the lists only read it, and every change goes through `apply`, which
 * keeps what it replaced, so `undo` can put it back.
 */
export const createSeating = (): Seating => {
  const state = reactive<Seating['state']>({
    tables: {
      a: [
        { id: 'ana', name: 'Ana' },
        { id: 'bo', name: 'Bo' },
        { id: 'cy', name: 'Cy' },
      ],
      b: [
        { id: 'di', name: 'Di' },
        { id: 'ed', name: 'Ed' },
      ],
    },
    history: [],
  });

  /** Writes a drop's `result`: the new arrays of every table it changes. */
  const apply = (result: ReadonlyMap<Key, Guest[]>, label: string) => {
    const before = [...result.keys()].map((id): [Key, Guest[]] => [id, state.tables[id]!]);
    for (const [id, guests] of result) state.tables[id] = guests;
    state.history.unshift({ label, before });
  };

  const undo = () => {
    const last = state.history.shift();
    for (const [id, guests] of last?.before ?? []) state.tables[id] = guests;
  };

  return { state, apply, undo };
};

<script setup lang="ts">
import { useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeSortableList } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';
import GuestRow from './GuestRow.vue';
import type { Seating } from './store';

const props = defineProps<{ id: string; title: string; seating: Seating }>();

const list = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('list');
// `items` is a getter: read-only, so the library never writes it. Each drop goes to the
// store instead: `preventDefault()` skips the write, and `e.result` holds the new arrays
// of every table the drop changes.
const { items, isOver } = makeSortableList(list, {
  id: props.id,
  items: () => props.seating.state.tables[props.id]!,
  group: 'seating',
  strategy: 'grid',
  onDrop: (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    const who = e.items.map((guest) => guest.name).join(', ');
    props.seating.apply(e.result, e.sameList ? `${who}: new seat at ${props.title}` : `${who} → ${props.title}`);
  },
});
</script>
